items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: I was taking from Maurice Grupp, the little sax player but he taught breathing

ctx.x: I’m interested in that, how that — what that was like going to Vietnam and playing those tours.

Well I told people that’s the highlight of my career because when I left Vegas, I ended up being in Vegas for six years. I played at The Dunes for four years. The other — there were two trumpets. One was Charlie Turner, who is an excellent trumpet player. He ended up traveling with Frank Sinatra for a couple of years, and myself. He had 60% of the lead, I had 40% approximately. A hard, hard book. That’s the hardest show I’ve ever worked in my life. It was music by the pound. And on one show, the first show we had…
I was wondering what the various conditions were like when you were playing for the service men and women in Vietnam. They would set up a stage for you and carry your own sound system?
